key_insight: GA-AMNO separates adaptive mesh learning into two interpretable parts: where to compute is chosen by physics, and how to interact is handled by geometry-aware gauge transport so features remain comparable across changing meshes.
engineering_relevance: This makes neural PDE solvers more reliable on nonuniform and dynamically adapted discretizations by reducing representation mismatch when meshes change.
method: Physics-informed adaptive mesh allocation selects sampling locations based on local PDE structure.
Geometry-conditioned low-rank Gauge transport maps source features into target representation contexts before aggregation.
Operator readability enables controlled interventions to test allocation vs. interaction effects separately.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports experiments on five PDE benchmarks, plus controlled interventions and geometric-mismatch analyses showing improved accuracy and better cross-discretization compatibility.
watch_item: Gauge transport adds an extra geometric modeling layer, so performance may depend on accurate mesh deformation estimates and stable low-rank transport under strong topology changes.
paper_title: Where to Compute and How to Interact: Operator-Readable Adaptation with Gauge-Aware Transport
